chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:

I asked him about a man who ate and drank after the dawn had emerged during the month of Ramadan. He said: If he stood up and looked, but did not see the dawn, so he ate, then returned and saw the dawn, let him complete his fast and there is no making it up again for him. And if he stood up and ate and drank, then looked to the dawn and saw that the dawn had emerged, let him complete his fast and he should compensate for it with another day, because he began with eating before looking, so upon him is the making up again.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if I eat breakfast after Fajr but before checking if the sun has risen?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'presumption of continuity' (istishab) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between negligence and genuine uncertainty regarding the onset of Fajr. It highlights the scholarly emphasis on due diligence, ruling that eating before verifying the dawn requires both completing the fast and making it up (qada), whereas verifying first exempts one from compensation. This ruling underscores the Shia legal focus on the intentionality of breaking the fast and the practical obligations of the fasting individual.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at Bin Mihran who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who eats and drinks after the emergence of the dawn during a Month of Ramazan. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was such that he stood and looked (outside for the dawn), but did not see the dawn, so he ate, then returned, so he saw the dawn, so let him complete his Fast, and there is no repeating upon him; but if it was such that he stood up and ate and drank, then looked to the dawn, so he saw that the dawn had emerged, so let him complete his Fast, and he should compensate for it another day, because he began with the eating before looking, so upon him is the repeating’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah ibn Mehran who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who eats and drinks after dawn in the month of Ramadan. He (the Imam) said, ‘If he got up and looked but did not see the dawn then ate then returned and saw that it was dawn, he is required to complete that fast and there is no Qada’ (compensatory fast) on him. If he gets up, eats and drinks, and then looks to the dawn that is already there, he is required to complete that fast and make Qada’ (compensatory fast) for one other day because he ate first, then went to find out about dawn, thus fast of one day is necessary.’”
